occupations.title: Electrician
occupations.summary: Installs, maintains and repairs the wiring, lighting, power and control systems of homes and buildings, working from drawings and the code, and tests the result.

procedures.name: Establishing an electrically safe work condition (lockout/tagout and test-before-touch)
procedures.purpose: Remove and prove the absence of hazardous electrical energy before anyone touches conductors or parts.
procedures.whenUsed: Before any repair, panel work, device change or troubleshooting that puts hands near conductors that could be energized.
procedures.role: Qualified electrician (apprentice under supervision), with the employer providing the written procedure, locks and tags.
steps: Identify every source of power to the equipment using drawings, labels and the panel schedule, including backfeed such as generators or second feeds.
Shut the load down with normal controls, then open the disconnecting means.
Visually confirm the disconnect is open, by handle position or visible blades.
Release or block stored energy (capacitors, batteries, springs, other non-electrical energy that could restart parts).
Apply your own lock and tag to each isolating device, per the employer's written procedure.
Test your meter on a known live source, then test the circuit conductors phase to phase and phase to ground, then re-test the meter on the known source (live-dead-live).
Apply temporary grounds where induced voltage or stored energy could remain a hazard.
Test before touching each conductor or part in the work area, work, then clear tools and people, remove your own lock, warn others and re-energize.
hazards: Shock and electrocution from missed backfeed or a second source
Arc flash if a meter or tool bridges live parts
Stored energy in capacitors or mechanical parts
A failed meter giving a false 'dead' reading
controls: Personal lock and tag on every isolation point, removed only by the person who applied it
Voltage test with a rated meter, proved before and after on a known live source
Written procedure and trained, authorized workers
Temporary grounds where induced voltage is possible
Insulated tools and PPE chosen for the task

procedures.name: Rough-in and finish wiring of a residential branch circuit
procedures.purpose: Install the boxes, cable, protection and devices of a new or extended branch circuit so it passes inspection and works safely.
procedures.whenUsed: New construction, additions and remodels where circuits are added or extended.
procedures.role: Journeyman or apprentice electrician under a licensed electrician or contractor.
steps: Work from the plans and load needs to lay out box locations, circuit routes and the panel location.
Set and fasten each outlet, switch and fixture box at the right height, using rated boxes where a fan or heavy fixture hangs.
Drill studs near their centers, run the cable, and protect it with nail plates where it is close to the face of framing.
Staple or support cable near every box and along its run at the code spacing.
Strip and terminate conductors in boxes, make splices and pigtails, connect grounding and bonding, and leave devices off.
Walk the job against the plan, checking support, box fill, circuit sizing and required GFCI and AFCI protection.
Request the rough-in inspection and keep the wiring uncovered until it passes.
After walls are finished, install devices and covers, make panel terminations, test the circuit (see testing procedure) and schedule the final inspection.
hazards: Nail or screw penetration of cable
Overfilled boxes and loose terminations causing heat
controls: Panel de-energized and locked out while terminating
Cable supported and protected per code
Proper box fill and device ratings

procedures.name: Installing or replacing a residential service panel
procedures.purpose: Replace or upgrade the main panel so the home has correct capacity, grounding and protection, with the utility and inspector involved.
procedures.whenUsed: Service upgrades, panel changeouts for age or capacity, and adding major loads such as EV chargers.
procedures.role: Licensed electrician or electrical contractor, with the utility doing its own disconnect and reconnect.
steps: Assess the existing service, decide the new panel size and circuit count, and check the load calculation.
Pull the permit from the local building department and schedule the utility disconnect and reconnect.
Gather materials and install ground rods or other grounding electrode parts ahead of time where possible.
On the scheduled day the utility cuts power; verify the service is dead, and lock out where possible, before opening anything.
Remove the old panel and mount the new one, install the service conductors and bond it to the grounding electrode system.
Land the branch circuits in the new panel, with correct breaker types and labelled directory.
Close up with covers and dead-front in place, and call for inspection.
After the inspector approves, the utility reconnects and you verify voltage and test the circuits.
hazards: Service conductors that may still be live up to the utility disconnect
Arc flash and shock when working in a panel
controls: Utility disconnect and verified dead conductors before work
Grounding electrode system and bonding done to code

procedures.name: Troubleshooting a dead or tripping circuit
procedures.purpose: Find the cause of a lost or tripping circuit with a systematic method and fix it without creating new hazards.
procedures.whenUsed: Service calls for dead outlets, nuisance trips, repeated breaker trips or burning smells.
procedures.role: Journeyman electrician, sometimes with an apprentice assisting.
steps: Ask what happened and observe: which outlets or lights are out, what trips, any smell, sound or heat.
Gather information: panel directory, circuit layout, recent work, GFCI or AFCI devices on the circuit.
Check obvious causes first, such as tripped GFCIs or AFCIs and breaker position, resetting only after considering why it tripped.
List the likely sections of the circuit and use a half-split approach, testing the middle to rule out half at a time.
Prove the meter on a known live source, test the dead point, and prove the meter again.
Isolate and lock out, then inspect and test the suspect parts (loose terminations, damaged cable, shorted or overloaded loads).
Repair or replace the faulty part with a correctly rated one.
Re-energize, verify operation under load, and note what was found.
hazards: Working live while looking for the fault
Arcing at a short or loose connection
Fire from a hot or damaged connection
Resetting a breaker into a fault
controls: Stop and escalate if there is a burning smell, a scorched device, instant re-trips or water
Half-split testing to limit live exposure

procedures.name: Testing and verifying a finished installation (continuity, polarity, GFCI and AFCI)
procedures.purpose: Show that a finished circuit is wired correctly and that its protective devices work before handing it over.
procedures.whenUsed: After devices are installed and before final inspection or turnover, and after any repair.
procedures.role: Electrician who did the work, or a second electrician checking it.
steps: Before energizing, confirm the circuit is deenergized, then check continuity of conductors and the grounding path with a meter (meter proved first).
Confirm connections: hot, neutral and ground landed on the right terminals and no shorts between conductors.
Energize and check voltage at the devices with a proved meter.
Plug in a receptacle tester to read correct wiring and polarity, and note any open ground or reversal.
Press the GFCI test button (or tester button): power must drop, then reset restores it.
Check downstream receptacles to confirm which outlets the GFCI protects and that line and load are not reversed.
Operate the AFCI breaker test button and confirm it trips and resets.
Record results and fix anything that fails before inspection.
hazards: Testing live circuits that were thought dead
False confidence from a plug-in tester
Reversed line and load on a GFCI
controls: Meter proven on a known source
Use the device's own test button for AFCI and GFCI
Document and correct failures before turnover

procedures.name: Conduit and cable installation
procedures.purpose: Install raceway and cable so conductors are protected, supported and can be pulled without damage.
procedures.whenUsed: Wherever the wiring method is conduit, in commercial, industrial and exposed residential work.
procedures.role: Journeyman or apprentice electrician.
steps: Pick the conduit type for the environment (metal for protected indoor runs, rigid for impact, PVC for wet or buried).
Mark box locations and support points from the drawings.
Cut conduit to length and ream the cut end so burrs do not damage insulation.
Bend with the correct bender, allowing for take-up, and keep total bends between pull points within the code limit.
Mount straps and supports at the required spacing and near every box.
Fit connectors and couplings, tighten metal fittings and add bushings where the conduit enters a box.
Fish and pull the conductors, using lubricant on long pulls, and keep conduit fill within the allowed percentage.
Check bonding continuity of metal raceways and leave the run ready for inspection.
hazards: Cuts and strains from cutting and bending
Insulation damage from burrs or overfill
Working near live parts while mounting
controls: Deenergize or guard live parts nearby

procedures.name: Load calculation and service sizing for a dwelling
procedures.purpose: Work out the demand on a home so the service, feeders and circuits are sized correctly.
procedures.whenUsed: New homes, additions, service upgrades and when adding large loads like EV chargers or ranges.
procedures.role: Electrician or contractor, sometimes checked by the plan reviewer.
steps: Take the floor area from outside dimensions (excluding open porches, garages and unfinished spaces) and apply the general lighting and receptacle load per square foot.
Add the required small-appliance and laundry circuits at the fixed volt-ampere value per circuit.
Combine those loads and apply the demand factors for the first block and the remainder.
Add fixed appliances, range, dryer, heating and cooling with their own demand rules, including a reduction when four or more fastened appliances exist.
Total the demand loads and divide by the service voltage to get amps.
Choose the standard service rating and size the service conductors, using the table allowed for the service.
Compare with the existing service where adding loads and document the calculation for the permit.
controls: Follow the code's worksheet method in order
Check results against the plan reviewer or utility requirements
Document the calculation with the permit

occupations.title: Solar installer
occupations.summary: Installs solar panels, wiring, inverters and disconnects on roofs and buildings, and tests and connects the system.

procedures.name: Site survey and roof fall protection
procedures.purpose: Assess the roof and site, then keep workers from falling during array installation.
procedures.whenUsed: Whenever work is at 6 feet or more above a lower level, which includes essentially all rooftop PV work.
procedures.role: Every crew member; the employer provides systems and training.
steps: Review plans and permit conditions and the adopted fire-code setbacks.
Walk the roof and check condition, slope, decking and attachment points.
Locate the service panel, meter, conduit routes and shading sources.
Identify overhead power lines, skylights, and roof edges and openings.
Inspect harness, lanyard or rope grab and connectors before use.
Install anchors into structural members, not sheathing alone.
Set ladder at a safe angle, secure it and extend it above the roof edge.
Connect to the anchor before stepping onto the roof.
Use guardrails or a safety monitor where the plan calls for them.
Keep tools and modules from sliding off the roof.
hazards: Slips on wet or dusty roofs
controls: Personal fall arrest systems, guardrails or monitored warning lines per the safety regulations
Ladder securing and three points of contact

procedures.name: Array installation, DC wiring and connector handling
procedures.purpose: Mount modules and wire strings with listed, correctly mated connectors and protected conductors.
procedures.whenUsed: During the main install phase after racking is set.
procedures.role: PV installers, with an electrician where state rules require.
steps: Set racking and attach modules per manufacturer instructions.
Cover or keep modules shaded when practical while wiring.
Mate connectors of the same listed type and check they are fully seated.
Route and secure PV wire and cable so it is protected from damage and abrasion.
Label and group strings as shown on the single-line diagram.
Run DC circuits in the approved wiring method to the combiner or inverter.
Seal roof penetrations and confirm conduit and box fittings.
Verify all work against the plan set before closing up.
hazards: DC arc from damaged or loose connectors
controls: Matched connectors and torque to manufacturer values
Module covering or shading while connecting

procedures.name: Inverter, combiner, disconnect and rapid shutdown installation
procedures.purpose: Place and connect conversion and shutdown equipment so the array can be isolated and firefighters are protected.
procedures.whenUsed: After array wiring, before commissioning.
procedures.role: Installer or electrician.
steps: Mount inverter and combiner in a code-compliant, accessible location per listing.
Install the PV disconnecting means and any required AC disconnect.
Install rapid shutdown devices or listed system components per manufacturer.
Wire the initiating device where the system needs one and place it per plan.
Connect overcurrent protection sized from the design.
Apply required rapid shutdown and warning labels.
Test the shutdown function and record the result.
hazards: Shock from DC and AC terminals
controls: Rapid shutdown limiting controlled conductors to low voltage within a set time
Listed shutdown equipment used per instructions

procedures.name: Grounding and bonding of the array
procedures.purpose: Bond all exposed metal and provide a fault path so ground faults are detected and cleared.
procedures.whenUsed: During racking and wiring, and verified at commissioning.
procedures.role: Installer or electrician.
steps: Use racking and bonding hardware listed for module bonding.
Bond module frames and rails per the hardware instructions.
Run the equipment grounding conductor from array to inverter and panel.
Size the EGC from the overcurrent device rating and protect small sizes from damage.
Connect any optional grounding electrode to the premises electrode system.
Confirm ground-fault protection is present in the inverter.
Test ground continuity before energizing.

procedures.name: Commissioning tests and electrically safe testing
procedures.purpose: Prove the installed system is correct and safe before energizing and handing over.
procedures.whenUsed: After installation, before inverter start-up and utility permission.
procedures.role: Installer or commissioning technician, often two people.
steps: Visually inspect wiring, labels, grounding and mounting with the system off.
Check meter on a known source, test, then recheck the meter.
Test continuity of grounding conductors.
Check polarity of each string at the combiner.
Measure open-circuit voltage per string and compare with temperature-corrected expected values.
Measure short-circuit current per string where the procedure calls for it.
Test insulation resistance with the disconnects open.
Start the inverter per manufacturer steps and verify AC side and shutdown.
Record results in the commissioning report.
controls: Test sequence with polarity before connection

procedures.name: Interconnection and utility hand-off
procedures.purpose: Connect the system to the building service and obtain utility permission to operate.
procedures.whenUsed: Design and permitting for the application; after inspection for permission to operate.
procedures.role: Installer company, electrician, inspector and the utility.
steps: Submit the interconnection application with equipment data.
Choose load-side or supply-side connection per panel limits.
Install the connection and the required plaque or directory at the service.
Obtain permit sign-off and pass the AHJ inspection.
Provide documents to the utility.
Wait for utility permission to operate before exporting.
Leave labels, as-builts and manuals for the owner.

procedures.name: Battery storage installation
procedures.purpose: Install energy storage with correct disconnects, protection, location and shutdown.
procedures.whenUsed: When a project includes batteries.
procedures.role: Electrician or manufacturer-certified installer.
steps: Confirm the unit is listed for battery storage and read its instructions.
Check allowed location and spacing with the fire code and AHJ.
Mount unit and install the lockable disconnect in sight or within the stated distance.
Size conductors and protection for continuous current.
Install the emergency shutdown device where required.
Label the system and apply any shock or arc warnings.
Commission and log maintenance records.

occupations.title: Electrician's helper
occupations.summary: Helps electricians by preparing materials, running wire and conduit and keeping the site safe, under supervision, while learning the trade.

procedures.name: Job-site electrical safety for a helper
procedures.purpose: Keep an unqualified worker away from energized parts and in the habit of asking first.
procedures.whenUsed: Every shift, and whenever a helper is near panels, exposed wiring, temporary power or overhead lines.
procedures.role: Helper (unqualified person) under an electrician or foreman
steps: Attend the pre-task briefing and learn which circuits and equipment nearby are live.
Put on required PPE and check it is in good, fitting condition.
Treat every conductor and terminal as live until the electrician says it is verified dead.
Never open, touch or work on energized equipment; ask the electrician first.
Keep the required distance from overhead lines and exposed energized parts.
Inspect cords, tools and temporary power and tag damaged items out of use.
Use GFCI-protected outlets or the site's tested grounding program for plug-in tools.
Stop and report any shock, burn smell, damaged insulation or unexpected energized part.
hazards: Shock and burns from live parts
Contact with overhead or buried lines

procedures.name: Assisting with lockout/tagout (what a helper may and may not do)
procedures.purpose: Ensure equipment is de-energized and cannot restart before anyone works on it, with the helper in the correct supporting role.
procedures.whenUsed: Before any work on or near equipment or circuits that could be energized or release stored energy.
procedures.role: Authorized employee (usually the electrician) applies and removes; the helper is an affected employee or, if trained, a group-lockout participant with a personal lock
steps: Electrician identifies every energy source and the hazards, and shares the plan.
Equipment is shut down by the normal method and notified people are told.
Each source is isolated at its disconnecting device.
Lock and tag go on every isolating device; a helper who is working puts a personal lock on a group device if their employer's program lets them.
Stored energy is released or blocked.
A qualified person verifies zero energy and tests with a meter, checking for backfeed.
Helper never removes another person's lock or tag and never restarts equipment.
Locks are removed only by the person who placed them after the area is clear and people are told.
controls: Group lockout with each worker's own lock
Training split between authorized and affected employees

procedures.name: Material handling and staging
procedures.purpose: Move and store conduit, cable, boxes and equipment without injury or creating site hazards.
procedures.whenUsed: At delivery, when staging for each run or room, and at end of shift.
procedures.role: Helper, with foreman direction
steps: Read the work plan to know what material goes where and in what order.
Check the route for aisles, openings, wet floors and overhead hazards.
Lift with legs, or use a cart or second person for long or heavy items such as conduit and spools.
Stack and block materials so they cannot slide, roll or fall; keep cylindrical items blocked.
Keep stored material away from floor openings and exterior edges.
Keep aisles and exits clear and separate incompatible materials.
Label and group materials by area or circuit for the electrician.
Return unused material to storage at end of shift.

procedures.name: Pulling wire and cable and running conduit under supervision
procedures.purpose: Get conductors through finished raceways without damaging them, with the electrician in charge of what is installed.
procedures.whenUsed: After raceways, boxes and fittings are installed and before termination.
procedures.role: Helper pulling and feeding, electrician directing and terminating
steps: Confirm with the electrician the conductor sizes, count and fill for the raceway.
Check the conduit run is complete, supported, cut and deburred, and clear of debris.
Feed a fish tape or pull line through by hand without forcing it.
Strip and bundle conductor ends and attach them to the tape or a pulling grip, tape smooth.
Apply pulling lubricant as the conductors enter; one person feeds while the other pulls.
Communicate during the pull and stop if it binds; back out and fix rather than forcing it.
Leave extra length at each box and label the conductors for the electrician.
Leave ends capped and do not terminate on energized circuits.
hazards: Hidden live circuits when drilling or cutting
controls: Fill limits from the code's conduit fill tables
Circuits verified de-energized before any connections

procedures.name: Layout, measuring and marking
procedures.purpose: Transfer plan locations onto the structure so boxes, conduit and equipment go in the right place.
procedures.whenUsed: Before drilling, boxing and running raceway.
procedures.role: Helper working from the electrician's marks or drawings
steps: Get the plan or marked locations from the electrician and confirm which version is current.
Check the area for existing wiring or pipes before marking or drilling.
Measure from fixed reference points and mark box and run locations clearly.
Mark conduit cut lengths and double-check before cutting.
Have the electrician verify the layout before drilling or boxing.
Record changes and tell the electrician of conflicts.

procedures.name: Using hand and power tools safely
procedures.purpose: Use drills, cutters and hand tools without shock, cuts or kickback and keep tools in safe condition.
procedures.whenUsed: Daily, for drilling, cutting, stripping and fastening.
procedures.role: Helper; powder-actuated tools only if trained
steps: Inspect each tool and cord before use and tag out damaged ones.
Use only double-insulated or grounded tools, on GFCI or tested power.
Wear eye and hearing protection and other required PPE.
Keep guards in place and use the right tool and bit for the material.
Secure the work and keep hands clear of the cutting path.
Never carry or lift a tool by its cord.
Do not use a powder-actuated tool unless trained; never leave one loaded and unattended.
Clean tools and return them to storage.

procedures.name: Ladder and fall safety
procedures.purpose: Reach work at height without falling and without contacting energized equipment.
procedures.whenUsed: Whenever work is above floor level, including ceilings, panels and roofs.
procedures.role: Helper and electrician, with a competent person inspecting
steps: Inspect the ladder for defects and remove it from service if damaged.
Choose nonconductive rails where energized equipment could be touched.
Set a non-self-supporting ladder at about one-quarter its working length from the base.
Extend the top 3 feet above the landing or secure it at the top.
Face the ladder and keep a hand on it; never carry loads that unbalance you.
Do not stand on the top step of a stepladder.
Use guardrails, covers or personal fall arrest at 6 feet or more at edges and holes.
Use stairways with railings as required.

procedures.name: Cleaning up and securing the site
procedures.purpose: Leave the area safe, free of trip and fire hazards, with energized equipment closed up and covered.
procedures.whenUsed: End of shift and end of each task.
procedures.role: Helper, checked by electrician or foreman
steps: Collect scrap, cut-offs and packaging and sort for disposal.
Clear aisles and working space around panels and equipment.
Return tools to storage and inspect them.
Cap or protect open conductor ends and boxes, per the electrician.
Close panels and covers; keep openings guarded or covered.
Barricade and sign any exposed energized equipment as directed.
Report damaged materials or hazards to the electrician.

occupations.title: Electrical inspector
occupations.summary: Inspects electrical work against the code and the plans, records what is wrong, and decides whether work can be approved.

procedures.name: Electrical plan review for a permit
procedures.purpose: Check on paper that a proposed electrical installation can be built to the adopted code before work starts.
procedures.whenUsed: At permit application for work that the jurisdiction requires plans for, such as larger services, multifamily, PV, generators, hazardous locations.
procedures.role: Electrical plans examiner, working with the permit technician and applicant.
steps: Confirm the permit application describes the work and that this job needs plan review under local rules.
Check the submittal is complete: floor or site plan, one-line or riser diagram, panel schedules, load calculation, and fault-current data where required.
Start at a branch circuit and follow the load path back to the service point, checking each conductor and device.
Compare the load calculation categories and demand factors with the equipment and conductor sizes shown.
Check short-circuit ratings of equipment against available fault current, and the grounding method shown on the riser.
Note whether a registered engineer's stamp is required for the occupancy or size.
Mark corrections for the applicant, or approve the plans and stamp the set for the field inspector.
hazards: Undersized service or feeders approved by mistake
Equipment rated below available fault current
Plans that differ from what is later built
controls: Engineer stamp for complex or life-safety systems
Field inspector compares installation to approved plans

procedures.name: New dwelling electrical inspection sequence
procedures.purpose: Inspect each hidden or critical part of the electrical work at the stage where it can still be seen and fixed.
procedures.whenUsed: Through construction of a new one- or two-family home, as the contractor requests each stage.
procedures.role: Field electrical or combination inspector, scheduled by the contractor.
steps: Temporary power pole: check it meets the code, including GFCI protection, before it is used.
Underground or slab: inspect conduit, in-slab wiring and the concrete-encased grounding electrode before concrete or backfill covers them.
Rough-in: after framing, fire blocking and bracing, check all wiring is run, secured and terminated in boxes, service cable and meter can are set, and splices made up.
Service and meter release: check the panel, disconnect and grounding electrode system, then release the meter or temporary power where the jurisdiction does this at rough-in.
Confirm earlier stages have passed before later ones (framing, insulation) are called.
Final: with fixtures, devices and panel cover in place, check protection devices, labels, smoke and CO alarms.
Record the result; the electrical approval feeds the certificate of occupancy.
hazards: Energizing before the service is approved
Uncovered boxes, open knockouts, unsupported cable at final
controls: Inspection requests tied to the permit
Readiness lists published by the jurisdiction

procedures.name: Service and panel inspection, including grounding and bonding
procedures.purpose: Confirm the service equipment, panel and grounding and bonding system are installed correctly before power is released.
procedures.whenUsed: At the service or meter-release inspection of a new service or upgrade, and again at final for items that need finished surfaces.
procedures.role: Field electrical inspector, with the contractor present to open the panel and supply a torque tool.
steps: Confirm the address and permit, and that the plans match the installed panel size.
Check working space in front of the panel and the mounting height of the highest device.
Check the enclosure is suitable for service equipment, breakers are listed for the panel, and conductor size matches the breaker.
Verify torque on lug and terminal connections with a calibrated tool.
Check grounded and ungrounded conductors are identified, and the neutral is bonded only where the code allows (service, not subpanels).
Check the grounding electrode system: electrode type, conductor size, accessible connections, all electrodes on site used, and bonding of water, gas and intersystem bonding termination.
Check cable clamps, no open knockouts, panel and conduit secured, and circuit labels.
Affix the compliance tag at the meter or panel and notify the utility, or fail the item and write the correction.
hazards: Arc flash if a cover is removed under load
Missing bonding leaving metal parts energized under fault
controls: Panel opened by the contractor with service off
Inspector uses PPE when energized parts are within reach
Checklist handed out so the contractor is ready

procedures.name: GFCI and AFCI verification
procedures.purpose: Confirm that required shock and arc-fault protection is installed in the right places and actually trips.
procedures.whenUsed: At final inspection of new work, and when a panel or circuits are changed.
procedures.role: Field electrical inspector, with the contractor supplying access to panels.
steps: Identify which areas and circuits need protection under the adopted code edition.
Look at each device or breaker visually for damage, looseness or heat marks.
Press the built-in test button on each protective device and confirm it trips and resets.
Use a GFCI receptacle tester on outlets to confirm the trip and to catch reversed line and load wiring.
Check outlets fed downstream of a GFCI are really protected and that AFCI circuits do not share a neutral.
Confirm devices are readily accessible and circuits are labeled.
Record failures as correction items by location.
hazards: Shock where protection is missing or miswired
Tripping a circuit and losing power to occupants' equipment
Testing a device while it is wired wrong gives false comfort
controls: Test with both the button and an outlet tester

procedures.name: Writing a correction notice, re-inspection, and approving or rejecting work
procedures.purpose: Record what failed, tell the contractor what must be fixed, and approve work only when it passes.
procedures.whenUsed: At the end of every inspection visit.
procedures.role: Field electrical inspector, then the permit office and utility.
steps: Go through the checklist item by item and note pass, fail or not ready, with photos when helpful.
For each failure, write the location, what is wrong and the code rule involved in plain words.
Result the inspection in the permit system as approved, partial or rejected, and leave a tag or notice on site.
Contractor fixes the items and requests re-inspection; the inspector checks the listed items and anything affected.
Apply the jurisdiction's re-inspection rules (for example a fee when the same item fails twice or the site is not ready).
On approval, affix the compliance label or sticker, update the record and notify the utility or permit office.
Keep records so the electrical approval is on file before the certificate of occupancy.
hazards: Unsafe work left in place if a failure is missed
Power released before corrections are done
controls: Release to utility only after approval

procedures.name: Inspector site safety and electrically safe work condition
procedures.purpose: Keep the inspector from shock, arc flash and fall injuries while looking at live or recently built electrical work.
procedures.whenUsed: Before any panel cover is removed, and when climbing or entering a construction site.
procedures.role: Inspector, with the contractor responsible for safe access and often for supplying PPE.
steps: Plan the visit: ask what is energized and arrange for the contractor to de-energize before the inspector arrives.
Do not remove covers from energized equipment unless it has been disconnected and verified safe.
Have the circuit disconnect locked out in the open position and tagged; a qualified person confirms de-energized with a tester.
If de-energizing is not possible, do an arc flash and shock risk assessment and use the required PPE, only as a qualified person.
Use a nonconductive ladder near energized parts, set at the right angle, extended three feet above the landing, three-point contact.
Watch for temporary wiring, damaged cords, overhead lines and tripping hazards on the site.
Leave energized equipment closed and report unsafe conditions.
hazards: Arc flash and shock when opening 120/240 V panels
Energized parts exposed in unfinished work
controls: Arc-rated PPE, insulating gloves, safety glasses

procedures.name: Checking code edition and local amendments
procedures.purpose: Make sure each inspection and plan review is judged against the code the jurisdiction actually enforces.
procedures.whenUsed: Before reviewing a permit, and whenever the state or local code is updated.
procedures.role: Inspector or plans examiner; the building official owns adoption.
steps: Find the adopted edition of the code for the jurisdiction and its effective date.
Check the state and the local ordinance for amendments, deletions or added rules.
Note the permit application date, since projects may be reviewed under the edition in force then.
Use the matching code book and handbook when citing a rule.
Share changes with contractors and train on new requirements.
Cite the section from the enforced edition on every correction notice.
hazards: Citing a rule from the wrong edition
controls: Ask the authority having jurisdiction when unsure

occupations.title: Fire and security alarm installer
occupations.summary: Installs and tests fire alarm and security systems: devices, panels, low-voltage wiring and their power supplies.

procedures.name: Electrically safe work for line-voltage connections
procedures.purpose: Make the supply to a panel, power supply or transformer dead and prove it before touching it.
procedures.whenUsed: Whenever a fire or security panel, power supply or other equipment is wired to or served from a line-voltage circuit.
procedures.role: Installer (qualified person) with the facility electrician or owner's authorized employee.
steps: Find the circuit that feeds the equipment and tell affected people the work is planned.
Switch off the circuit and open the disconnecting means; for fire alarm panels note that this removes protection, so arrange impairment steps first.
Apply a lock and tag to the disconnect, or use the equivalent measure if a lock cannot be fitted.
Release or restrain any stored energy, including backup batteries on the panel.
Test with a meter that works, check the circuit at the work point, then recheck the meter.
Do the work, keeping to required approach distances and using insulated tools.
Before restoring power, remove tools, check people are clear, remove locks and tags, then re-energize and confirm normal status.
hazards: Loss of fire protection while the panel is off
controls: Insulated tools and PPE chosen by hazard assessment
Impairment notification when a fire system is off

procedures.name: Plan reading and device layout check
procedures.purpose: Work out where devices, panels and cable runs go and which circuits they use before pulling cable.
procedures.whenUsed: At job start, from the work order, drawings and building plans.
procedures.role: Installer or lead installer, with the designer or project manager.
steps: Read the work order and scope, and confirm the system type (fire, intrusion, access control, video).
Check the approved shop drawings and device layout against the building plans.
Mark panel, power supply, device and annunciator locations, checking mounting and access space.
Plan cable routes, noting fire-rated walls, ceilings and spaces where firestopping or plenum cable is needed.
Identify each circuit's class (power-limited fire alarm, Class 2/3, non-power-limited, communications) and plan separation from power wiring.
List materials and quantities, and raise conflicts with the designer before drilling.
hazards: Drilling into live wiring or structure
Wrong cable type in a plenum or fire-rated assembly
controls: Layout reviewed with designer or inspector

procedures.name: Running low-voltage and fire alarm cable and raceway
procedures.purpose: Route, support, separate and identify signaling cable so it stays safe and trouble-free.
procedures.whenUsed: During rough-in, for new work and additions.
procedures.role: Systems installer or technician, working to the plans and the employer's written procedure.
steps: Choose cable of the right listed type for the circuit and the space (riser, plenum, general).
Keep fire alarm and Class 2/3 conductors out of enclosures and raceways with power or Class 1 conductors unless separated by a barrier or the approved exception applies.
Route through or along framing with the specified clearance or a protective plate.
Support cable with secure fastening at the required intervals and keep the work neat.
Firestop penetrations through fire-rated assemblies.
Label circuits at junction points so other work does not trigger signals, and remove abandoned cable.
Check the run for damage before termination.
hazards: Cable damage or short against power conductors
Shock hazard if a fault crosses to line voltage

procedures.name: Installing panels, devices and power supply connections
procedures.purpose: Mount and connect panels, detectors, notification devices and security devices, and supply the panel correctly.
procedures.whenUsed: Trim-out after rough-in.
procedures.role: Installer; a licensed electrician may do the line-voltage feed depending on the state.
steps: Mount the panel and power supply at the planned location with working space and access.
Confirm the feed comes from a dedicated branch circuit with a marked disconnect and no ground-fault or arc-fault protection where the code forbids it.
Connect devices and terminate conductors, keeping circuit polarity and supervision correct.
Ground metal enclosures and connect equipment grounding conductors.
Install batteries last, only when ready to test.
Mount detectors, horns, strobes, pull stations and sensors at the layout locations.
Label the panel, circuits and the feed disconnect.
controls: Procedure 1 before work on the feed
Dedicated, marked fire alarm branch circuit

procedures.name: Programming, addressing and sensitivity adjustment
procedures.purpose: Make devices known to the panel and set them so they report correctly without false alarms.
procedures.whenUsed: After device installation and before testing, and after changes.
procedures.role: Installer or programming technician.
steps: Assign addresses or zones to each device per the point list and drawings.
Enter device types, labels and zone text in the panel from the approved sequence of operations.
Set outputs, notification and monitoring communication settings.
Adjust detector sensitivity to the room within the allowed range.
Back up the programming and record the version.
Check that each point shows the correct label before functional testing.
hazards: Wrong zone leading to wrong location reported

procedures.name: Functional and acceptance testing with documentation
procedures.purpose: Show every device and the standby power work, and record the result for the authority having jurisdiction and owner.
procedures.whenUsed: After installation and programming, and again after any added, deleted or modified components.
procedures.role: Installer or certified technician, with the owner and the authority having jurisdiction (AHJ) or inspector.
steps: Confirm approved drawings, sequence of operations and the battery calculation are on hand.
Check wiring and insulation for faults and verify circuit supervision by creating open and ground conditions.
Test pull stations, smoke and heat detectors by approved methods, and supervisory inputs such as waterflow and tamper.
Verify audible and visible notification appliances operate across the coverage area.
Test standby battery condition and capacity and check the system survives the required standby period.
Confirm alarm, supervisory and trouble signals reach the panel, annunciators and monitoring service.
Record deficiencies and correct them, reset to normal, and obtain the inspector's sign-off.
Deliver records and train the owner.
hazards: False dispatch to the fire department
Shock from live equipment during testing
controls: Notify monitoring company and building occupants before testing

procedures.name: Impairment handling and restoration
procedures.purpose: Control the risk and tell the right people when a fire alarm system or part is out of service.
procedures.whenUsed: When a system is turned off for service, a fault takes devices out, or work lasts beyond a short period.
procedures.role: Impairment coordinator (owner or designated person) with the service technician.
steps: Notify the coordinator before the system is taken out of service and agree scope and duration.
Inform the fire department, owner, insurer and monitoring company as the plan requires.
Use a fire watch or other interim measures for longer outages.
Tag the affected equipment as out of service.
Complete the repair and run the tests needed to prove the affected parts work.
Notify all parties that protection is restored and remove the tag.
controls: Notification to the fire department and others

occupations.title: Power-line installer
occupations.summary: Builds and maintains the lines, poles, transformers and cables that carry power from the utility to customers.

procedures.name: Job briefing and hazard assessment
procedures.purpose: Make sure every crew member knows the hazards, plan, controls and protective equipment before work begins.
procedures.whenUsed: Before each shift or job, and again whenever conditions change significantly.
procedures.role: Crew leader (employee in charge) with the whole crew
steps: Gather available information on the system: voltages, grounding, switching status, environment and nearby hazards.
Walk or patrol the site and note hazards such as traffic, weather, vegetation, induced voltage and other lines.
Hold the briefing: describe the work, hazards, procedures, special precautions, energy-source controls and protective equipment.
Assign roles, including who requests clearances and who is the first-aid and rescue person.
Confirm every member understands, and fit the depth of the briefing to how complex or unfamiliar the task is.
Re-brief when scope, crew or conditions change; a worker alone still plans as if a briefing were required.
hazards: Miscommunication between crew and system operator
controls: Documented or verbal briefing each shift
Two first-aid trained persons on field crews

procedures.name: De-energizing, testing, grounding and tagging lines
procedures.purpose: Make a line or device safe to touch by isolating it, proving it dead and grounding it, with tags showing who is working.
procedures.whenUsed: Before working hands-on with lines or equipment that can be taken out of service.
procedures.role: Designated employee in charge with the system operator and crew
steps: Designated employee requests that the system operator de-energize the specific line or equipment section and takes responsibility for the clearance.
Open and secure switches and disconnects; apply tags (and locks where possible) that forbid operation and show crews are working.
Tag automatic and remote-controlled switches at their control points too.
After the operator confirms clearance, test each conductor with a voltage detector to prove it is dead.
Install protective grounds, attaching the ground end first with live-line tools, to cover stray or induced voltage and backfeed.
Work under the clearance, keeping the hold tags in place.
To restore, clear crews, remove grounds in reverse order, release the clearance and remove tags, then the operator re-energizes.
hazards: Backfeed from generators or tie switches
controls: Tags and locks at every point of isolation
Grounds sized to carry fault current, conductor ampacity at least that of No. 2 AWG copper

procedures.name: Working near and on energized lines (approach distances)
procedures.purpose: Keep qualified workers from reaching live parts that cannot be de-energized, by distance or insulation.
procedures.whenUsed: Live-line work, work from bucket trucks near conductors, and any operation near exposed energized parts.
procedures.role: Qualified line workers in a team
steps: Confirm only qualified employees do the work and that the voltage is known.
Determine the minimum approach distance for the voltage and altitude from the standard's tables.
Choose the method: stay out of the distance, insulate the worker, or insulate the live part from other objects.
Put on arc-rated clothing and insulating gloves with sleeves, donning and removing them only outside the approach distance.
Remove conductive jewelry; use insulated aerial devices or live-line tools as the method requires.
Keep at least two qualified people on most energized work above 600 volts, with exceptions such as routine switching and emergencies.
Connect de-energized parts to energized circuits at the de-energized end first when joining, and disconnect at the source end first.
controls: Insulating rubber gear and live-line tools

procedures.name: Climbing, fall protection and aerial-lift work
procedures.purpose: Keep workers from falling while on poles, towers and in bucket trucks.
procedures.whenUsed: Whenever working above about 1.2 m on poles or structures, and from aerial devices.
procedures.role: Line worker, with ground person and crew leader
steps: Check that the pole or structure can carry the added and unbalanced load; brace or support it first if not.
Inspect climbing gear, body harness, positioning strap and lanyard before use.
Select protection: fall arrest, work positioning or restraint, as feasible.
Attach to a suitable anchorage and keep the connection through the climb or lift.
In a bucket, wear the harness tied to the boom or basket and keep insulated devices clear of energized parts.
Keep people from standing under the work and secure tools and loads.
hazards: Contact with energized parts while at height
controls: Fall protection equipment inspection and rated anchorages

procedures.name: Setting poles and stringing conductors
procedures.purpose: Place new or replacement poles and pull wire between structures without contacting energized lines.
procedures.whenUsed: New construction, rebuilds and storm replacement of overhead lines.
procedures.role: Line crew with equipment operator and ground crew
steps: Locate the line and nearby energized conductors; plan equipment positions and clearances.
Guard or attend pole holes and keep the digger, derrick and load from touching energized parts.
Handle poles near live lines only with protective equipment or insulated devices; no bare-hand contact.
Use tension stringing or barriers so the new conductor cannot touch energized lines; disable automatic reclosing where crossing above energized conductors over 600 V.
Assess induced voltage from parallel lines and install temporary grounds so workers are not exposed to potential differences.
Control towers and loads with tag lines; keep people out from under loads.
Check sag, clearances and hardware against the design before energizing.
hazards: Contact between pole or conductor and live lines

procedures.name: Underground cable and vault work (enclosed spaces)
procedures.purpose: Work on buried cable and in manholes or vaults without atmospheric, electrical or rescue hazards.
procedures.whenUsed: Underground distribution cable splicing, transformer vault and manhole entry.
procedures.role: Cable crew with an attendant outside the space
steps: Locate and mark the cable and other utilities; identify the cable to be worked on.
Open the cover and evaluate pressure, temperature and other hazards before entry.
Test for oxygen deficiency first, then flammable gases and vapors, with direct-reading instruments.
Ventilate with forced air if a hazard is found; keep ventilation running.
Station a trained, first-aid qualified attendant outside with rescue equipment.
De-energize and ground the cable per the de-energizing procedure, or work it with proper cable-handling tools.
Splice or repair, restore covers and release the clearance.

procedures.name: Storm restoration and outage switching
procedures.purpose: Find damage, isolate faulted sections and return service safely after an outage.
procedures.whenUsed: After storms, faults and equipment failures, often with long hours and mutual-aid crews.
procedures.role: Line crews, system operator, damage assessors
steps: Assess damage section by section, treating every downed or low line as energized until proven otherwise.
Keep the public away and mark and guard the work zone with signs, cones or barricades.
Isolate the faulted section through the system operator by opening switches and applying tags.
Test, ground and clear the section per the de-energizing procedure; watch for backfeed from generators and tie points.
Repair or replace poles, wire and equipment, sometimes from aerial lifts or in confined spaces.
Release clearances and tags, confirm everyone is clear, then have the operator re-energize in sequence.
hazards: Downed energized wires energizing fences or objects

procedures.name: Making and verifying a service connection and meter at the customer
procedures.purpose: Connect the utility service drop or lateral to the customer's service equipment and confirm the connection and metering are correct and safe.
procedures.whenUsed: New service, service upgrades, meter changes, and reconnects.
procedures.role: Utility line worker or meter technician, with the customer's electrician
steps: Confirm the service point and that the customer's installation has passed inspection or been released by the authority having jurisdiction and utility rules.
Check the meter socket, service entrance conductors, grounding and labeling on the customer side look complete.
Make the line-side connection to the service drop or lateral under the utility's de-energized or live-line procedure.
Install the meter or current-transformer metering and seal it.
Verify voltage and phasing with a meter before and after closing the service.
Leave deficiencies, such as missing grounding or bonding, for the customer's electrician and decline to energize if unsafe.
hazards: Shock and arc at the meter socket
controls: Service point defined by utility rules
